svg.title: Valve surgery decision chart: leaky (regurgitant) valves are repaired where possible, tight (stenotic) valves are replaced; severe aortic stenosis is replaced surgically when the patient will live more than 5 to 7 years or by transcatheter implantation in elderly moderate-to-high-risk patients; a replacement valve is mechanical (durable, lifelong anticoagulation) or bioprosthetic (no anticoagulation, wears out in about 15 years), chosen by age, anticoagulation risk and conditions that wear tissue valves out
